intro: WRL source, its canonical form, and two hosts that each compute what it means.

steps.caption: The starter world: a pulser, a relay, a spinner and an orb, three routes. Canonicalized.
Host A hashes the canonical form: sem-67e954cf…. Host B, independently: sem-67e954cf…. That id is the meaning.
steps.takeaway: The semantics of a world is its SemanticArtifactID: computed, on every host, forever.

steps.caption: Edit one route. The canonical form changes, so the meaning changes, so the hash changes.
Both hosts agree again — on a different id. There is no version flag to consult; the hash is the version.
steps.takeaway: A change of meaning is a change of hash; a preserved hash is a preserved meaning. There is nothing else to check.

steps.caption: Unison did this for functions; Nix for packages. The prior-art field says so; the contribution here is executable topology plus refusal names on the wire.
steps.takeaway: Direct prior art exists and is credited — the page's Prior art field answers 'is this a renaming?' honestly.
